q: Higher Inductive Types (HITs) in HoTT can define the circle S¹ with:
opts: One point constructor base: S¹ and one path constructor loop: base = base
Two point constructors and one path
exp: S¹ as a HIT: base: S¹ (a point), loop: base = base (a non-trivial path). HoTT proves π₁(S¹) = ℤ—the fundamental group of the circle—purely type-theoretically. This demonstrates topology via HoTT without appeal to sets.
